tema: Commentary on the scientific and clinical milestones that have increased the legitimization of ME/CFS in the last decade.
diseno: Commentary/editorial; no empirical data.
hallazgos: Milestones: government reports on its severity, NIH research initiatives, adoption of the name ME/CFS, guidelines for professionals and a new fatigue journal; stigma, lack of markers and treatments, and a shortage of researchers persist.
conclusion: There has been progress in legitimacy, attributable to the advocacy of patients and professionals, although challenges remain in achieving full legitimacy.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add the author's declaration of ties to several of the milestones cited.

tema: Proposes that the persistence of ME/CFS reflects a stable pathological balance in endocrine-immune regulation (HPA and HPG axes) and explores treatment-relevant phenotypes in women.
diseno: Mechanistic model based on literature on endocrine-immune co-regulation, fitted to experimental exercise data and analysed through computer simulations; population not stated.
hallazgos: The simulations support an aetiology in which sustained overactivation of the HPG axis would allow peripheral inflammation to be initiated and maintained with possible low-grade neuroinflammation; the partial efficacy of rituximab and rintatolimod is predicted as an alteration of the steady-state landscape that reduces the availability of pathological states.
conclusion: Studies and trials in women should consider the menstrual cycle, and HPA and HPG hormones (cortisol, ACTH, oestrogen, GnRH, LH) could help develop biomarkers and delimit subgroups responsive to treatment.
triangulacion: The abstract is the opening text (includes the author header) but is consistent with the keywords and conclusions on HPA/HPG axes and rituximab; the conclusions provide the simulation results absent from the truncated abstract.

tema: Describes a CFS patient in whom the cranial venous drainage obstruction model guided the work-up and surgical treatment.
diseno: Case report; CT and catheter venography.
hallazgos: Focal stenoses of both jugular veins and of the left brachiocephalic trunk were identified; the brachiocephalic obstruction was not treatable, but surgical release of the jugular obstruction, in successive procedures, produced incremental, significant clinical improvements, lasting during follow-up.
conclusion: Investigating CFS under this model could benefit specific patients and provide knowledge about idiopathic intracranial hypertension and its relationship to spontaneous intracranial hypotension.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion are consistent with the model of venous obstruction and CSF leak; the available discussion is brief and mostly administrative noise, so the weight falls on the abstract.

tema: Studies regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) in ME/CFS using arterial spin labelling.
diseno: Case-control study with PCASL on 3 T MRI in 31 patients and 48 healthy controls; voxel-wise and AAL ROI comparisons and regression with symptom severity.
hallazgos: Patients showed significant hypoperfusion in limbic regions (anterior cingulate cortex, putamen, pallidum and anterior ventral insula); symptom severity was associated with lower rCBF in the anterior cingulate cortex.
conclusion: Blood flow abnormalities in the limbic system could contribute to the pathogenesis of ME/CFS and PCASL is useful for studying them.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on limbic hypoperfusion and the anterior cingulate; the conclusions qualify that the correlation with symptoms (EQ-VAS) was only significant in a small cluster.

tema: Uses long-read sequencing to characterize a structural variant at the AKR1C locus in a case of unexplained severe fatigue and proposes a new aetiology.
diseno: Single-case study with nanopore sequencing to resolve a large inversion in a highly homologous region of the AKR1C locus, unresolved with short reads; serum steroid analysis by GC-MS/MS.
hallazgos: Several bioinformatic tools are confused by the homology, but a combined approach with visual inspection resolved the variant. The inversion appears to increase AKR1C2 expression and limit AKR1C1 activity, with a relative increase in inhibitory GABAergic neurosteroids and altered progesterone metabolism.
conclusion: Long-read sequencing can improve diagnostic yield; overactivation of AKR1C2 with partial loss of AKR1C1 could be a new pathology underlying some cases of chronic fatigue, with biomarkers and treatments (UDCA, sepranolone, golexanolone) to be evaluated in larger cohorts.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and PDF conclusions are consistent on structural variants, AKR1C1/AKR1C2 and long reads; the conclusions are conditional and call for confirmation in other patients, and mention therapeutic candidates absent from the abstract.

tema: Evaluates long-term symptom severity and clinical biomarkers in post-COVID syndrome (PCS) with fatigue, comparing those who meet ME/CFS criteria with those who do not.
diseno: Prospective observational cohort in 106 PCS patients with moderate-severe fatigue and exercise intolerance (Charité, Berlin, 2020-2022), evaluated at 3-8, 9-16 and 17-20 months; handgrip strength, cardiovascular function and laboratory parameters; PCS-ME/CFS subgroup according to Canadian criteria (CCC).
hallazgos: PCS-ME/CFS patients maintained high severity of most symptoms up to 20 months, whereas PCS improved. Fatigue and PEM persisted in both groups, more marked in PCS-ME/CFS; inflammatory markers decreased, but antinuclear antibodies did not, and lower initial handgrip strength correlated with persistence.
conclusion: PCS can persist beyond 20 months and encompass the full spectrum of post-infectious ME/CFS; subclassifying with the CCC helps management and follow-up.
triangulacion: The conclusions come from the abstract, so they agree fully (and include funding text); the keywords (PEM, handgrip strength, inflammatory markers) are consistent with the study's focus.

tema: Analyses the long-term course of neuropsychological symptoms and ME/CFS after SARS-CoV-2 infection.
diseno: Registry study from a German university centre with 1022 post-COVID patients, 411 with more than one visit; comparison of symptoms and structured neuropsychological screening between the first and second visit.
hallazgos: 95.5% had a polysymptomatic illness. 31.3% met ME/CFS criteria at the first visit (median 255 days) and 19.4% at the second (median 402 days). Self-reported fatigue (83.7% to 72.7%) and concentration problems (66.2% to 57.9%) decreased, with no significant changes in the structured screening.
conclusion: A significant proportion of survivors with persistent symptoms have ME/CFS; although subjective symptoms decrease, many patients remain affected and new therapeutic concepts and specialized interventions are needed.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent. The discussion only provides a final sentence calling for prospective studies and interventions; the rest is noise from contributions, funding and licence.

tema: Practical guide from the Bateman Horne Center to prepare for and cope with crash/PEM episodes in ME/CFS.
diseno: Guide for patients, support network and healthcare team prepared by eight professionals affected by ME/CFS.
hallazgos: Provides information on PEM, advance preparation for crash episodes and adaptations in daily activities to conserve energy.
conclusion: Not stated (no conclusions text available).
triangulacion: Only the opening text is available; there are no keywords or conclusions, so the analysis is limited to the stated purpose of the guide.

tema: Examines whether memory problems in CFS reflect slower responses.
diseno: Case-control study with 67 CFS patients from a specialist clinic and 126 healthy volunteers; tasks of immediate recall, delayed recognition, logical reasoning and semantic processing.
hallazgos: Patients recalled fewer words and had poorer delayed recognition; in the other tasks they were slower but without loss of accuracy.
conclusion: The poorer recognition probably reflects the poorer immediate recall, and slowness could explain part of the recall deficit.
triangulacion: There are no keywords. Abstract and conclusions agree on slowness; the conclusions speak of impaired performance in reasoning and semantic processing, whereas the abstract indicates only slowness without affecting accuracy.

tema: Suggests that methylation alterations from MTHFR variants connect long COVID, CFS, POTS, MCAS, SIBO and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
diseno: Hypothesis article and biochemical review of the folate and methionine cycles; no own data.
hallazgos: Proposes that female preponderance, fatigue, chronic inflammation and MTHFR abnormalities unite these syndromes, with oxidative stress, mitochondrial overload, antioxidant and nutrient deficits and a suboptimal microbiome as determinants. Active vitamin D and vitamins B2, B3, B6, B9 and B12 would be key for methylation.
conclusion: The six syndromes could be related phenotypes triggered by epigenetic hypomethylation due to abnormal MTHFR, with homocysteine as a marker; vitamin D and magnesium deficits and the value of an antioxidant-rich diet are highlighted.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on MTHFR, methylation and overlapping syndromes. The conclusions add the role of magnesium and extend the hypothesis to ageing, cancer and cardiovascular disease; it is a speculative model without own empirical data.

tema: Evaluates whether machine learning applied to fMRI can differentiate CFS from Gulf War illness (GWI).
diseno: fMRI during a 2-back task before and after exercise in 80 subjects with GWI and 38 with CFS; AAL regions and an ensemble of machine learning algorithms with feature selection.
hallazgos: The models differentiated CFS from GWI with a mean accuracy of 75% before and 79% after exercise; the best individual models reached 82%, and the combination of six or more models 100%. The right anterior insula, putamen, prefrontal cortex and parietal and temporal regions were involved.
conclusion: CFS and GWI are distinguishable with an fMRI activity pattern based on a machine learning model; more data are needed.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on differential diagnosis and activation patterns; the conclusions are somewhat more cautious and call for larger samples.

tema: Updates the neuropsychological and neuroimaging features of the cognitive disorder associated with macrophagic myofasciitis (MMF).
diseno: Commissioned, peer-reviewed narrative review; number of studies not stated.
hallazgos: The cognitive disorder associated with MMF affects attention, executive functions and short- and long-term memory, sometimes with left auditory extinction. MRI is usually uninformative, but SPECT and PET show a pattern involving posterior associative areas, temporal lobes, the limbic system and the cerebellum.
conclusion: The data support an organic origin of the disorder; the authors propose investigating the cognitive phenotype, comparing functional imaging with ME/CFS and looking for genetic factors in response to aluminium adjuvants.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree on neuropsychology and functional imaging; the conclusions open onto the context of vaccine safety and add practical points and a research agenda.

tema: Describes the management of a post-viral neuropathic POTS with craniosacral therapy.
diseno: Case report of a 39-year-old man with post-viral POTS treated with osteopathic manipulative treatment, specifically fourth ventricle compression (CV4).
hallazgos: The CV4 technique was associated with remission of the patient's symptoms.
conclusion: The authors propose craniosacral therapy (CV4) as a management modality for POTS, alone or as an adjunct to conventional therapy.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent, although the generalization of the conclusions exceeds what a single case allows; the small fibre neuropathy keyword reflects the proposed mechanism, not demonstrated in the case.

tema: Examines fatigue in POTS, its prevalence, its overlap with CFS and the Newcastle clinical management approach.
diseno: Narrative review or clinical chapter; search methodology not stated.
hallazgos: Fatigue is frequent in POTS and of diverse causes; there are no evidence-based pharmacological treatments and, even with heart rate control, not all patients improve their fatigue.
conclusion: An individualized, multidisciplinary approach adapting strategies from other conditions is recommended, along with more research on the causes of fatigue and specific therapeutic options.
triangulacion: The abstract is actually opening text of the document, but agrees with the keywords and discussion on fatigue, POTS and management; the discussion qualifies the lack of evidence and the off-label use of many drugs.

tema: Review (part two) on the mechanisms linking chronic HPA axis activation, inflammation and chronic fatigue.
diseno: Narrative review in French; no methodology stated.
hallazgos: Acute HPA axis activation mobilizes energy and suppresses fatigue, whereas its chronic activation reduces muscle efficiency and leads to chronic fatigue; dysbiosis, infectious origin and long COVID are discussed.
conclusion: There is a parallel between inflammation and acute or chronic fatigue: the acute form is useful and the chronic one deleterious; the transition mechanisms are not well understood.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree on the HPA axis, stress and inflammation; the conclusions text mixes sections on Alzheimer's, dysbiosis and long COVID, broader than the abstract's focus.

tema: Examines brain structural variations associated with sleep quality in CFS.
diseno: Cross-sectional study in 38 CFS patients and 14 controls; MRI with volumes, magnetization transfer (MT) and T1/T2 intensities; PSQI, CFQ and HADS; regressions adjusted for age, anxiety and depression.
hallazgos: In patients there were negative correlations between PSQI and MT-T1w and T1w intensities in the medial prefrontal cortex, where these intensities were also lower than in controls (uncorrected).
conclusion: The integrity of the medial prefrontal cortex could be affected; the finding refutes that unrefreshing sleep is a misperception and justifies further research.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on unrefreshing sleep and the medial prefrontal cortex; the conclusions add that the discrepancy with objective measures would be because traditional methods do not capture the mechanism.

tema: Meta-analyses the association between PEM and a diagnosis of ME/CFS versus controls and its moderators.
diseno: Meta-analysis of odds ratios with study-level moderator analysis; number of studies not stated.
hallazgos: PEM was 10.4 times more likely in ME/CFS than in controls; the recruitment strategy and the selection of controls significantly moderated the effect size.
conclusion: PEM should be considered a cardinal symptom of ME/CFS, able to distinguish between people with and without the disease; greater collaboration and methodological standardization are called for.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions add emphasis on the value of meta-analysis for empirical case definitions, in line with the keywords on case definition and control selection.

tema: Mini-review of metabolic abnormalities in CFS/ME as possible biomarkers.
diseno: Brief narrative review on immune dysregulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, AMPK activation, muscle acidosis and metabolomics. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Possible biomarkers are identified: cytokines, mitochondrial changes, muscle abnormalities after exercise, AMPK activation and metabolic alterations; the data are contradictory between studies.
conclusion: The aetiopathogenesis remains unclear; multicentre and multidisciplinary research is required to obtain robust data and establish whether the metabolic changes are cause or consequence.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree. The conclusions stress more the lack of reproducibility between studies as a limitation for identifying biomarkers.

tema: Looks for a chemical signature of CFS through targeted plasma metabolomics.
diseno: Case-control study (UC San Diego, 2014-2015): patients meeting IOM 2015, Canadian and Fukuda criteria, and controls matched for age and sex (22 men with CFS and 18 controls; 23 women with CFS and 21 controls); targeted plasma metabolomics and ROC analysis.
hallazgos: Diagnostic accuracy exceeded 90% (AUROC 0.94 in men with 8 analytes and 0.96 in women with 13). The pattern indicates a conserved hypometabolic response to stress, similar to the dauer state; about 25% of the alterations were enough for diagnosis and 75% were individual.
conclusion: CFS has an objective chemical signature that reduces diagnostic uncertainty and could guide personalized treatments, although it requires validation in larger cohorts and against disorders such as depression or PTSD.
triangulacion: The abstract is not useful (generic journal text), so the analysis is based on the conclusions (with noise from methods and tables) and general keywords consistent with the metabolic focus.

tema: Determines whether subjective dysautonomia measured by questionnaires correlates with the objective dysautonomia of quantitative autonomic tests.
diseno: Retrospective cross-sectional study (2017-2023) at an autonomic laboratory; 2627 patients with SAS, QASAT and CASS and 564 with COMPASS-31; Valsalva, deep breathing, sudomotor test and tilt table; diagnostic subgroups, among them 95 with ME/CFS.
hallazgos: The correlation was strong between subjective instruments (r = 0.74) and between objective ones (r = 0.81), but there was no correlation between subjective and objective, nor by diagnosis (post-COVID, POTS, ME/CFS, hEDS, among others).
conclusion: Autonomic questionnaires have limitations, with patients overestimating or underestimating the deficit, and cannot be recommended as a substitute for autonomic testing.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions are shorter and call for studying the origin and meaning of subjective dysautonomia. ME/CFS is only one of the subgroups analysed.

tema: Reviews the biological bases of ME/CFS focusing on the mitochondria of immune cells and their interaction with other systems.
diseno: Narrative literature review; the available abstract is the opening text of the article.
hallazgos: Describes the interactive roles of the microbiome and intestinal permeability, the endogenous opioid system, immune cell mitochondria, the autonomic nervous system, microRNA-155, viral infection or reactivation, leptin, melatonin and the circadian rhythm.
conclusion: The gut and immune cell mitochondria would be two key hubs that interact with the circadian regulation of immune and glial activation; modulation of immune/glial mitochondrial function would be crucial for integrating the data on ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, opening text and conclusions are consistent on mitochondria, immunity, gut and the opioid system. The conclusions add underfunding because of poor conceptualization and extrapolation to fibromyalgia, depression, dementia and migraine.

tema: Reviews mitochondrial dysfunction in post-viral fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS, fibromyalgia, long COVID) and the efficacy of coenzyme Q10 supplementation.
diseno: Critical literature review on mitochondrial dysfunction and intervention studies with CoQ10. No sample stated.
hallazgos: The literature links mitochondrial dysfunction with low-grade systemic inflammation in ME/CFS, FM and long COVID. Questions remain about CoQ10 bioavailability, routes of administration, blood-brain barrier crossing and co-supplementation.
conclusion: Mitochondria-dependent pathways would be an attractive therapeutic target and interventions based on combined CoQ10 appear achievable in the medium term.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree on mitochondria and CoQ10; the conclusions (from the discussion, with contribution noise) focus on research gaps. It is notable that one author is an adviser to a company in the sector, which qualifies the optimism.

tema: Published version of the exploratory study comparing qualitative interviews and VAS to measure PEM after a CPET in ME/CFS.
diseno: Exploratory mixed-methods study with 10 ME/CFS patients and 9 healthy individuals; VAS for 12 symptoms and semi-structured interviews at six time points over 72 h; Spearman correlations.
hallazgos: Each patient had a unique PEM in onset, severity and trajectory; no healthy individual developed PEM. The VAS-interview correlation for fatigue was good before the CPET (r=0.7) and poor at peak PEM (r=0.28), improving with the most bothersome symptom.
conclusion: The interviews were more sensitive to PEM change than the VAS; a mixed approach can optimize the subjective assessment of PEM.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent and almost identical to paper 4 (earlier version with 7 symptoms). The conclusions are brief and cautious, stressing their exploratory nature.

tema: Evaluates whether management decisions for unruptured intracranial aneurysms changed after the implementation of the PHASES score.
diseno: Retrospective study at two Dutch tertiary centres (UMCU and LUMC), 2011-2017; 623 patients with 803 aneurysms, analysis per aneurysm.
hallazgos: The proportion with a decision to treat fell from 34.2% to 26.4% after implementation (absolute difference -7.8%), mainly in those under 50 (-22.3%) and only at the UMCU (-10.6%).
conclusion: Management changed after PHASES implementation, with a different impact by age and centre; the effect needs to be confirmed and ruptures, complications and quality of life evaluated.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent with each other, but the paper does not deal with ME/CFS or the batch's topic; it appears to be a document included in the collection by mistake.

tema: Letter describing a case of Parkinson's disease after COVID-19 and suggesting that the infection made a prodromal Parkinson's symptomatic.
diseno: Letter to the editor with one case (64-year-old woman with PCR-confirmed COVID-19 and resting tremor at 5 days) studied with DaTscan, and review of published cases.
hallazgos: The patient had minimal hypomimia and mild left bradykinesia and rigidity, with reduced uptake in the right putamen on DaTscan, compatible with Parkinson's disease.
conclusion: The authors propose a prodromal Parkinson's unmasked by the biological or psychological stress of COVID-19 and also the possibility of post-encephalitic parkinsonism; until the aetiopathogenic correlation is established, these cases should be interpreted with caution.
triangulacion: The keywords (prodromal Parkinson's, psychological stress) agree with the opening text and the discussion. The discussion broadens the mechanisms (encephalitis, olfactory hypothesis, hypoxic damage) and is explicitly cautious; ME/CFS does not appear in any source.
